method: See FRAME-INSPECTION-METHOD.md. Each clip's 12-frame contact sheet at resources/corpus/raw/mat-av-min/contact-sheets/<id>.jpg was inspected directly. person is split into 'real' (a photographed human) and 'rendered' (an animated or illustrated character) because an identity-preservation result measured on a rendered character is not evidence about a photographed face.
inspector: RES-005 worker, direct inspection of the committed contact sheets

MAVM-01.seen: Rendered animal characters (rabbit, squirrel, butterfly) against a tree and meadow. One continuous shot. No manufactured object, no titles.

MAVM-02.seen: Rendered humanoid character and a creature across four shots, wide to close-up. Strong camera and subject movement. No titles in this window.

MAVM-03.seen: Photographed actor's face in profile, eye at a scope. A manufactured prop weapon is held across frame in several shots. Four shots alternating scope-POV and the actor. The only clip in the set with a photographed human face AND a held object.

MAVM-04.seen: A rotorcraft test article hovering in a controlled indoor chamber against fabric walls. One locked shot, no people in frame, no titles.

MAVM-05.seen: Two photographed presenters in a studio, both faces visible and speaking. A labelled spectroscopy chart with axis text and a WEBB SPACE TELESCOPE wordmark are rendered on the wall behind them. Rendered text over live action.

MAVM-06.seen: A large rendered TW@N / This Week @NASA title card, a hard cut to a photographed auditorium of people, and burnt-in caption text across the lower third. Rendered titles and captions over documentary footage.

MAVM-07.seen: A slow horizontal pan across Martian terrain, colour grade shifting through the window. No people, no manufactured object near enough to read, no titles. Its value here is unambiguous directional camera motion for the frame-reversal perturbation.

MAVM-08.seen: The Ingenuity helicopter standing on the Martian surface in colour, across two shots at different scales. Hardware clearly readable in frame. No people, no titles.

MAVM-09.seen: Motion-graphics explainer. A rendered WIKIMEDIA FOUNDATION wordmark with connected icons, then illustrated human figures across several scene changes. The cleanest rendered type in the set, at 3840x2160 - the best available base for the text-mutation perturbation.

MAVM-10.seen: Illustrated human figures and hands across six shots, with a rendered 'The Wikimedia Alliances Fund' title held on screen. NOTE: assumed before inspection to be a talking-head video; it is animation. The tag was corrected from the sheet, not from the title.

MAVM-11.seen: A photographed human hand and forearm holding a branded cookware pot over a sink. A burnt-in Japanese caption naming the product sits top-left throughout. A face is never visible, so this clip supports product-swap but NOT identity-swap.

MAVM-12.seen: A commercial coffee machine dispensing into a cup, camera pushing in. Product wordmarks (KREA, NECTA) and menu labels are PHOTOGRAPHED signage on the machine itself rather than rendered overlay - a useful contrast with the rendered-text clips, because photographed and rendered text fail differently.
